_comment: One TTFV receipt per reader per track. Fill by hand following docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md; delete no keys. Null means not reached, not applicable, or unknown. Save as docs/measurement/receipts/YYYY-MM-DD-<handle>-<track>.json. track: demo | own-agent. date: YYYY-MM-DD of the attempt. facilitator: a handle only, no personal data. network: yes | no, whether the machine had internet access during the attempt; required yes for Track A and for uv tool install; checked once before the clock starts (protocol 2.7). coaching_events: list of {"at", "what"}. failures: list of {"at", "milestone", "what"}, kept even when the attempt failed.

reader._comment: handle: a public handle, no other personal data. kind: cold | maintainer | ai-agent; only cold receipts without coaching events count toward cold-reader metrics.

machine._comment: os and cpu as reported by the system (e.g. uname -sr, CPU model and core count); python and uv are `python3 --version` and `uv --version`. uv_cache: cold (fresh UV_CACHE_DIR) or warm.

package._comment: version: the agent-reliability-ci version installed. source: pypi or wheel. wheel_sha256: required when source is wheel (record UV_FIND_LINKS and any UV_CACHE_DIR in notes, protocol 2.3). readme_url: the README read, at a fixed commit.

project._comment: Track B only; null for demo. kind: own | sample. description: what the agent is, or which recipe the sample tree came from. refs_preexisting: baseline, candidate, toolset and oracle were importable before the clock started. workers: worker count of the run.
project.description: examples/recipes/python_agent copied to a temporary directory, arci.yaml removed; project dir /var/folders/2k/b4x5xvk54w36pjwr4kxjgx7w0000gn/T/tmp.7Qzi7C36lY/python_agent

timestamps._comment: ISO 8601 with timezone, e.g. 2026-10-20T09:15:02Z. Track A uses readme_opened, command_start, demo_banner, demo_verdict, all_steps_held, interpretation_answered. Track B uses readme_opened, install_start, install_done, scaffold_start, descriptor_written, run_start, verdict_printed, store_validated, interpretation_answered. Leave the others null.

durations_seconds._comment: Whole seconds derived from the timestamps as the protocol defines per track (sections 3 and 4). agent_execution is Track B only: the sum of usage.wall_seconds over trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2), never subtracted from total.

outcome._comment: completed: every stop condition of the track held. verdict: PASS | BLOCK | INCONCLUSIVE | ERROR; Track B: the verdict stamped as verdict_printed; ERROR if none; Track A: the verdict for agent B. store_validated, decision_sha256, init_attempts, descriptor_hand_edited, trials_started: Track B only (protocol 4.3 and 4.6). descriptor_hand_edited: arci.yaml edited by hand before the run that produced the verdict, or, with no valid verdict, before any arci run that started trials. trials_started: trials.jsonl in the run store (protocol 4.2) exists and is non-empty. interpretation_correct is scored with the key in protocol 5.3.
outcome.interpretation_answer: INCONCLUSIVE (exit 2): with only 8 trials per arm (the smoke design), v1 got 8/8 and v2 got 2/8, but the bounds on the difference [-0.9779, 0.1160] cross -delta. So the gate can neither show non-inferiority nor claim a regression. It says this N cannot tell, not that v2 is safe. The tool suggests using arci plan to pick a larger confirmatory N (the sample says about 400 per arm) and running that as a new experiment. Re-running `arci gate` on the store gave the same verdict, and decision.json kept the same sha256.

comprehension._comment: Answered once per reader, on the first track's receipt; on a second-track receipt set answered_on to that file name and leave the rest empty. Answers verbatim; scores per the key in protocol section 5; scorer is not the reader and is a handle only, no personal data. q2_who_for keeps its name for schema stability; it holds the whole q2 answer (who it is for and what the agent must expose).

coaching_events.what: Facilitator prompt stated, before the clock, that this harness blocks `uv tool install` and that uvx or a uv venv are alternatives; it also prescribed the timestamping wrapper and the milestone names. No explanation of ARCI was given.

notes: Install method: uv venv + uv pip install (README's `uv tool install agent-reliability-ci` was blocked by the harness). Venv at /var/folders/2k/b4x5xvk54w36pjwr4kxjgx7w0000gn/T/tmp.GTkCSURpx3/venv (uv picked CPython 3.13.12), agent-reliability-ci==0.8.0 from PyPI, venv bin prepended to PATH.. AI-agent reader (Claude opus via the Workflow tool, persona: a backend engineer who ships Python services and has used pytest and GitHub Actions for years); self-stamped milestones with `date -u` under the facilitator's wrapper; machine shared with the orchestrator session (not controlled). Never counted as a cold reader. Files read: /Users/ajay/Developer/agent-reliability-ci/README.md, <copy of examples/recipes/python_agent>/README.md (/var/folders/2k/b4x5xvk54w36pjwr4kxjgx7w0000gn/T/tmp.7Qzi7C36lY/python_agent/README.md), <copy>/tests/world.py, <copy>/app/v1.py, <copy>/app/v2.py, <copy>/arci.yaml (the one arci init generated), <copy>/run.out, run.err, gate.out (my own command output), /var/folders/2k/b4x5xvk54w36pjwr4kxjgx7w0000gn/T/tmp.e9n3mAxfqz/demo.log (via tee). Confusions: The README's 'Gate your own agent' command (arci init with only the four references) does not work for this toolset: make_world needs task['order_id'], and init calls it with a default task, so it fails with KeyError 'order_id'. The README mentions --task '{...}' only in passing in the next paragraph and never says the default task is empty. I had to open the sample project's own README and world.py to find the right --task value. | The README's own command has no --fault, so it would write a clean condition with no injected fault. I added --fault tool_timeout:reserve:0 because the sample README asks for it. The main README's example says `--fault tool_timeout:reserve` without the occurrence, so I was not sure which form is canonical. | Every link in the README points to github.com, not to local relative paths, so a reader with the checkout cannot tell which local docs/ files are 'linked'. I did not open any docs/ file. | The sample README links ../../../docs/measurement/ttfv-protocol.md (off limits; not opened). It also says 'Until agent-reliability-ci is on PyPI', which contradicts the main README saying v0.8.0 is on PyPI. | The demo's 'ok' lines and the 'All six steps held' ending are clear. The relationship between alpha/(4K) in STATISTICS and the '97.5%' per-arm confidence shown in the table was not obvious to me as a newcomer. | The README talks about a 'System One decision endpoint (TypeSafe's Jev API)' with no explanation. For a first-time visitor it is unclear whether that is relevant to a normal Python agent (I concluded it is not). | uv chose CPython 3.13.12 for the venv, although the environment notes say Python 3.14 is on PATH. It worked, but I did not choose it.. Reader notes: Timing: README opened 12:05:40Z, and the demo started 12:05:44Z. The banner appeared at 12:05:45Z (uvx resolved quickly, so the package seemed cached already), the B verdict at 12:06:09Z, and 'All six steps held.' at 12:06:58Z (about 74 s). Track B's install took about 1 s (packages were in uv's cache: 'Installed 7 packages in 7ms'), so this is not a cold-network install time. Scaffold took under 1 s; the run took about 2 s (12:07:33Z to 12:07:35Z). From README opened to the validated gate verdict was about 2 minutes (12:05:40Z to 12:07:40Z), including the demo. My time was inflated by the blocked install and the failed first init, but I read fast, so a human would take longer to read the README. After both demo runs, load average was 7.85/4.63/2.82 (the demo uses 8 workers); I saw no other arci processes before Track B. The demo printed counts matching the recorded run (A 192/200, B 132/200; A vs A PASS; A vs C PASS). Smoke run: v1 8/8, v2 2/8, one failure cluster (6 failures, first_failed_tool=reserve:timeout), as the sample README predicts. The sample README's first-screen command differs from the main README's: it adds --task and --fault. Without them the main README's command fails on this project, which is the main friction point for a cold reader. I did not run arci plan, diff, minimize, bundle or replay. The demo's store dirs are left in /var/folders/.../T/arci-demo-8gz8tdo_ and arci-demo-joletzn3.
